**Uptime Tiers:**
- Enterprise: 99.99% monthly uptime

rows.name: SLA tiers
rows.text:
Based on the SLA document I found, here are the uptime tiers and corresponding credit levels for the Northstar Platform:

## Uptime Tiers and Credits

**Availability Tiers:**
- Enterprise: 99.99% monthly uptime
- Professional: 99.9% monthly uptime
- Starter: 99.5% monthly uptime

**Service Credits:**
- 99.9-99.99%: 10% credit
- 99-99.9%: 25% credit
- 95-99%: 50% credit
- <95%: 100% credit

The SLA also specifies that credits are calculated based on the difference between the actual uptime achieved and the guaranteed uptime tier. For example, if an Enterprise customer receives 99.98% uptime instead of the guaranteed 99.99%, they would receive a 10% credit for that month.

Note: The SLA excludes credits for scheduled maintenance (Sundays 2-6 AM PST with 72-hour notice), customer-caused issues, force majeure events, third-party outages, and beta features.

rows.name: Onboarding steps
rows.text:
Based on the Northstar Technologies New Engineer Onboarding Checklist, here are the key tasks a new engineer should complete during their **first week**:

## Day 1: Getting Started
**IT & Access Setup:**
- Receive laptop and equipment from IT (contact: Thomas Young, IT Manager)
- Set up corporate email ({EMAIL})
- Configure multi-factor authentication (MFA) using Okta Verify app
- Complete security awareness training module in Workday Learning
- Sign acceptable use policy and NDA documents in DocuSign

**Account Access Requests (submit via IT Portal):**
- GitHub Enterprise access - request from your manager
- AWS Console access - request from David Kim (DevOps)
- Jira project access - request from your team lead
- Confluence wiki access - automatic with email setup
- Slack workspace - invitation sent to corporate email
- DataDog monitoring access - request from David Kim
- PagerDuty access (for on-call rotation) - request from Sarah Chen

**Communication Setup:**
- Join Slack and introduce yourself in #engineering-general
- Join team-specific Slack channels:
  - #engineering-general
  - #engineering-alerts
  - #deployments
  - #incident-response

## Additional First Week Tasks:
- Read through the coding style guide in Confluence
- Understand the PR review process and approval requirements
- Set up code review notifications in GitHub
- Attend sprint planning meeting
- Attend engineering team meeting (Thursdays 10 AM)

The checklist indicates that Week 2 includes deeper dive tasks like picking up your first ticket, submitting your first pull request, and participating in code reviews, but the items listed above should be completed during the first week of onboarding.
